senses.d: A portable or wearable timepiece.
ex: Meronyms: watch face, watch receiver, watchspring, watch battery, watchstrap, watch strap, watchband
He set the alarm on his watch to 8:00 am.

senses.d: The act of guarding and observing someone or something.
ex: shepherds keeping watch by night
All the long night their mournful watch they keep.

senses.d: A particular time period when guarding is kept.
ex: The second watch of the night began at midnight.
I did stand my watch upon the hill.

senses.d: A period of wakefulness between the two sleeps of a biphasic sleep pattern (the dead sleep or first sleep and morning sleep or second sleep): the first waking.
A person or group of people who guard.
ex: The watch stopped the travelers at the city gates.
Pilate said unto them, Ye have a watch; go your way, make it as sure as ye can.

senses.d: The post or office of a watchman; also, the place where a watchman is posted, or where a guard is kept.
ex:
He upbraids Iago, that he made him
 Brave me upon the watch.

senses.d: A group of sailors and officers aboard a ship or shore station with a common period of duty: starboard watch, port watch.
A period of time on duty, usually four hours in length; the officers and crew who tend the working of a vessel during the same watch. (FM 55–501).
The act of seeing, or viewing, for a period of time.
A group of nightingales.
ex: sirens were singing like a watch of nightingales
it was as if sunshine and a watch of nightingales had come into a sombre forest

senses.d: To look at, see, or view for a period of time.
ex: Watching the clock will not make time go faster.
I'm tired of watching TV.

senses.d: To observe over a period of time; to notice or pay attention.
ex: Watch this!
Put a little baking soda in some vinegar and watch what happens.

senses.d: To mind, attend, or guard.
ex: Please watch my suitcase for a minute.
He has to watch the kids that afternoon.

senses.d: To be wary or cautious of.
ex: You should watch that guy. He has a reputation for lying.

senses.d: To attend to dangers to or regarding.
ex: watch your head; watch your step
Watch yourself when you talk to him.

senses.d: To remain awake with a sick or dying person; to maintain a vigil.
ex: At the funeralls in Yorkeshire, to this day, they continue the custome of watching & sitting-up all night till the body is interred.

senses.d: To be vigilant or on one's guard.
ex: For some must watch, while some must sleep: So runs the world away.

senses.d: To act as a lookout.
To serve the purpose of a watchman by floating properly in its place.
To be awake.

Made of or covered with material that doesn't allow water in; impervious to water and immune to its effects.
Incapable of failing; unassailable.

To make waterproof or water-resistant.
A substance or preparation for rendering cloth, leather, etc., impervious to water.
Cloth made waterproof, or any article made of such cloth, or of other waterproof material, as rubber; especially, an outer garment made of such material.
ex: Carrados dropped the near window as a man in glistening waterproof stepped from the shelter of a lich-gate and approached.

A waterfall-like outpouring of liquid, smoke, etc.
ex: A waterfall of mist came from the open freezer.

The action of drinking from a vessel without touching it with the lips, considered more sanitary for a shared vessel.
ex: Hey man, can I take a waterfall from your bottle?

senses.d: A necktie.
A chignon (hairstyle).
A beard.
ex: I found home a dreary place after my long absence; for half the children I had known were now wearing whiskers or waterfalls, […]

senses.d: A kind of handstand with chin tucked and back arched.
To fall like a waterfall.
ex: Rain ran off the bill of his fielder's cap and waterfalled in front of his face.
Zondra, whose dirty-blond hair waterfalled above her head from a colorful tie, gave a snorting, horsey kind of laugh.

A critical point marking a change in course or development.
ex: watershed moment — watershed event — watershed ruling
In the minds of many, 1847 was a watershed year during which Ceres, Pallas, Juno, Vesta, and Astraea were reclassified as asteroids.

senses.d: An inorganic compound (of molecular formula H₂O) found at room temperature and pressure as a clear liquid; it is present naturally as rain, and found in rivers, lakes and seas; its solid form is ice and its gaseous form is steam.
ex: By the action of electricity, the water was resolved into its two parts, oxygen and hydrogen.

senses.d: The liquid form of this substance: liquid H₂O.
ex: May I have a glass of water?
Your plants need more water.

senses.d: A serving of liquid water.
ex: Joe bustled back and offered her a glass of wine but she shook her head. “Just a water, please.”

senses.d: The aforementioned liquid, considered one of the Classical elements or basic elements of alchemy.
ex: He showed me the river of living water, sparkling like crystal, flowing from the throne of God.

senses.d: Water in a body; an area of open water.
ex: The president expressed hope that creating rain over waters between the countries would help reduce pollution.
And God said, Let the waters under the heaven be gathered together unto one place, and let the dry land appear: and it was so.

senses.d: A body of water, almost always a river, sometimes a lake or reservoir, especially in the names given to such bodies.
ex:
On one side lay the Ocean, and on one
Lay a great water, and the moon was full.
But ere he came to Clyde's water, fu' loud the wind did blaw.

senses.d: Mineral water.
ex: Perrier is the most popular water in this restaurant.

senses.d: Spa water; hot springs.
ex: Many people visit Bath to take the waters.

senses.d: A solution in water of a gaseous or readily volatile substance.
ex: ammonia water

senses.d: Urine.
ex: Ser Dunaver's squire Jodge could not hold his water when he slept.

senses.d: To wet or supply with water; to moisten; to overflow with water; to irrigate.
ex: tears watering the ground
Men whose lives glided on like rivers that water the woodlands.

senses.d: To pour water into the soil surrounding (plants).
ex: Aunt Em had just come out of the house to water the cabbages when she looked up and saw Dorothy running toward her.

senses.d: To provide (animals) with water for drinking.
ex: I need to water the cattle.
While they watered and washed their horses, I talked with a red-capped man, some kind of chief.

senses.d: To provide water to (someone).
ex: We fed and watered the refugees.

senses.d: To urinate onto.
ex: Nature called, so I stepped into the woods and watered a tree.

senses.d: To fill with or secrete water or similar liquid.
ex: Chopping onions makes my eyes water.
The smell of fried onions makes my mouth water.

senses.d: To get or take in water.
ex: The ship put into port to water.

senses.d: To gather water.
ex: We stopped at the same well we watered at on the last journey.

senses.d: To dilute.
ex: Can you water the whisky, please?

senses.d: To treat with water.
ex: The town waters the dirt road for dust prevention.
